Whoever seeks ease must first believe in Allah and His Messenger, resolve himself to obey them, and begin to act upon that obedience. Second, he must spend in the way of Allah, by which he purifies himself from the disease of stinginess (shuh) and miserliness of the soul, and shows his poverty and need of Allah by drawing near to Him through voluntary acts and righteous deeds. By this he will have actually been made easy for the path of ease.

As for His saying, ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life)﴾, that is, the (present) world. Accordingly, whoever seeks it from other than Us has erred and will by no means obtain it. Seeking the Hereafter is by faith and piety, and seeking this world is by action, according to Our way in earning and acquiring wealth.

As for His saying, ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes. No one will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾: that is, on the basis of what We have explained to you, I have warned you, that is, made you fear, a Fire that blazes, flaring up intensely, which no one will enter and be scorched by its heat, remaining in it forever, except the most wretched, that is, the one with the greatest wretchedness, who is the polytheist. A wretched one from among the people of tawhid may enter it, but will leave it by virtue of his tawhid, since he did not deny and did not turn away; rather he sinned and disobeyed, but he did not associate partners with Allah and did not turn away.

As for His saying, ﴿But the most righteous will be kept far from it, the one who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾: that is, he gives his wealth in the way of Allah, purifying himself by it from the disease of stinginess and miserliness and from the traces of sins and wrongdoing.

He does not spend in order that someone among people has a favour or a hand (yad) upon him that he would repay with it. No, rather he spends seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High, that is, he wants only the good pleasure of his Lord, the Exalted.

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾: that is, as long as he spends seeking only Our Face, We will reward him and give him a gift with which he will be satisfied, and that is in Paradise, the Abode of Peace.

This noble verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). He used to buy slaves in Makkah from their masters who were torturing them because of their Islam. Allah refuted them in this and revealed His saying, ﴿And the most righteous will be kept far from it﴾, and the verses that follow.
